programme: NFE2L2 (NRF2) driving the canonical antioxidant-response module (NQO1, GCLC, GCLM, GSR, PRDX1, HMOX1, SLC7A11, GSTP1, KEAP1) together with HSF1 driving the heat-shock/proteotoxic-stress module (HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1, HSPA4, HSPA9, HSPA1A, HSPB1, SERPINH1), with NUPR1 acting as the integrated-stress-response node (ATF4, TP53, CDKN1A, BCL2L1) and ENO1 supplying the glycolytic/Warburg metabolic arm — together a redox-proteotoxic-metabolic stress-adaptation network.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this network is the classic cytoprotective response to ischemia-reperfusion and oxidative vascular injury: NRF2/KEAP1-ARE signalling and HSF1-driven heat-shock proteins buffer cardiomyocytes and endothelium against ROS and misfolded-protein stress during hypoxic insult, with glycolytic flux (ENO1) sustaining ATP under reduced oxygen delivery.
role_in_b: In colorectal cancer the same axis is repurposed for tumor survival and progression: NUPR1 confers ferroptosis and radioresistance and is described as a central stress-adaptation node integrating metabolic rewiring and cell death (PMID 42104400, 40176685, 41820294); ENO1 drives aerobic glycolysis and a lactate-PD-L1 axis that supports progression and immune evasion (PMID 42523085, 42491336, 42632257, 42554628); HSF1 promotes malignant phenotype via super-enhancer-driven transcription (PMID 41173249, 40162508); NFE2L2 sits at the 97th percentile of Open Targets association for this cancer, consistent with its known tumor-supportive antioxidant-buffering role, though no usable PMID for it was retrieved here.
shared_axis: Ischemic/hypoxic cardiovascular tissue and the hypoxic, nutrient-poor colorectal tumor microenvironment impose overlapping oxidative, proteotoxic, and metabolic stress; the same NRF2-HSF1-NUPR1-ENO1 network that protects stressed cardiac/vascular cells is co-opted by tumor cells facing comparable stress, which would explain why these factors' target sets recur concordantly across many independently-derived patient groups in both diseases despite the diseases sharing no organ or clinical pathway.
reasoning: The module is cleanly nameable from canonical, non-overlapping target sets (ARE genes, HSPs, ATF4/apoptosis genes, glycolytic/EMT genes) and three of its four carrying factors are independently placed in colorectal cancer by direct, on-topic PMIDs. But every factor in the entire list — including all four carrying factors — has zero retrieved evidence or Open Targets association for cardiovascular disease, so the cardiovascular side of the story rests on established general knowledge of ischemia-reperfusion biology rather than on anything in this record.
support: PMID 42104400 — NUPR1 as a central stress-adaptation node integrating metabolic rewiring and cell death (cancer, general framing of the module); PMID 40176685 — NUPR1 promotes radioresistance in CRC by inhibiting ferroptosis; PMID 41820294 — CDX2 upregulates NUPR1 to confer ferroptosis resistance in colon cancer; PMID 41873218 — NUPR1 and LCN2 as CRC therapeutic targets via cell viability/metabolism; PMID 42523085 — UFMylation of ENO1 restrains aerobic glycolysis and CRC progression; PMID 42491336 — NAT1-ENO1-lactate axis destabilizes PD-L1 in CRC; PMID 42554628 — circRNA-FXR1 histone lactylation promotes CRC; PMID 42632257 — gut microbiome-butyrate-ENO1-lactate axis and anti-PD-1 response in CRC; PMID 41173249 — HSF1 super-enhancer lncRNA drives malignant CRC phenotype; PMID 40162508 — HSF1 promotes CRC progression via CLDN3 transactivation. No PMID above supports any factor in cardiovascular disease.
how_to_falsify: In parallel, pharmacologically inhibit NRF2 (e.g. ML385) and HSF1 (e.g. KRIBB11) in (1) a cardiomyocyte/endothelial ischemia-reperfusion model and (2) a colorectal cancer hypoxic spheroid or xenograft model, tracking the shared downstream targets (HMOX1/NQO1/GCLC, HSPA/HSPB genes, ATF4, ENO1-dependent lactate output). If the two systems fail to show concordant loss of stress tolerance and concordant downstream target suppression — e.g. CRC cells are HSF1/NRF2-dependent but cardiac cells are not, or vice versa — the shared-programme account is wrong.
caveats: 152 patient-group comparisons from 4 independent cohort pairs across an unusual blood/colorectal tissue pairing. Tissue-generic exclusions removed general inflammatory/stress TFs (FOS, JUNB, CEBPD, BCL3, RUNX2, SMAD3, STAT5B, TAL1, EBF1, IRF8, VDR, E2F3), so this account cannot and should not reach for a generic 'blood or colon master regulator' — none of those are available, which is by design, not omission. Eight of the twelve concordant factors (STAT6, BCL11B, ZBTB2, HBP1, OVOL1, ZNF224, POU2AF1, ISL1) were deliberately left out of the carrying set: they span immune/differentiation, B-cell, and cardiac-pancreatic developmental functions that do not integrate with the redox-proteotoxic-metabolic module named here, and forcing them in would overstate coherence. Zero retrieved evidence places any factor, including the four carrying ones, in cardiovascular disease — the analysis notes this is due to a restrictive disease-A query, so it should be read as a retrieval gap, not disproof, but it means the CVD half of this account is unverified by the record in hand.
